reasons: Cached opinion header: '322 U.S. 143 (1944)', 'ASHCRAFT ET AL. v. TENNESSEE', 'Supreme Court of United States', 'Decided May 1, 1944' — matches citation, court, year and date_decided.
Lake cluster 103981 carries parallel '64 S. Ct. 921' / '88 L. Ed. 1192' and neutral '1944 U.S. LEXIS 782'; official_selection selected '322 U.S. 143'.

Justice Black's majority holds 36-hour relay interrogation 'so inherently coercive that its very existence is irreconcilable with the possession of mental freedom' under Fourteenth Amendment due process — a foundational anchor for due-process voluntariness of confessions.
'The Constitution of the United States stands as a bar against the conviction of any individual in an American court by means of a coerced confession' squarely anchors the topic.

Cached opinion: 'For thirty-six hours after Ashcraft's seizure during which period he was held incommunicado, without sleep or rest, relays of officers... questioned him without respite,' then 'We think a situation such as that here shown by uncontradicted evidence is so inherently coercive...'.
'Our conclusion is that if Ashcraft made a confession it was not voluntary but compelled' confirms the resulting confession was rendered involuntary — matching the (truncated) holding.
